title.title: Bose–Einstein condensation at positive temperature
title.subtitle: Claim: the dilute 3D hard-sphere Bose gas condenses in the thermodynamic limit at some fixed temperature $T > 0$

beats.text: Dilute hard-sphere bosons: the fraction in one quantum state, against the gas parameter
The curve: the claimed Bogoliubov depletion law, to leading order
Headline claim: a positive fraction still condenses at a fixed $T > 0$

achievement.label: Bose–Einstein condensation of an interacting gas
achievement.context: Before: proofs only in scaling limits; even $T = 0$ in the thermodynamic limit was open
achievement.note: $T$ is small and not located; hard spheres at small fixed density

verify.detail: Lean: ground-state BEC for the dilute hard-sphere gas. Not the $T > 0$ theorem

plain: Cool a gas and many atoms pile into one shared state; this claims it happens for real, colliding atoms

steps: Picture the gas as random loops of particle paths
Bound how often the loops run into each other
So long loops hold a fixed share: the gas condenses

voice.text: Dilute colliding hard spheres: what fraction of the particles shares a single quantum state?
Write the gas as random loops; long loops carry a fixed share.
Claimed: condensation at a fixed positive temperature.
